_comment: Shape reference for the remediation playbook. GENERAL guidance per vulnerability
class -- how this kind of defect is fixed anywhere, never how this application's
specific line is fixed. The moment an entry describes one call site it stops being
guidance and starts being the answer.
`preserve` and `common_mistakes` are the two fields that earn their keep: the first
is the only part of the guidance that argues for the feature, and the second names
the plausible-but-wrong fix before the agent invents it.
general_guidance: Fix at the trust boundary, not at the symptom. Prefer a change that makes the unsafe construction impossible over one that filters the unsafe input. Keep the feature: every endpoint here exists because something legitimate calls it, and a remediation that stops the legitimate caller has traded one defect for another.

entries.title: Injection
entries.guidance: Separate code from data. Send the query structure and the user-supplied values to the interpreter over different channels -- parameterised statements, bound replacements, or an ORM's typed query builder -- so a value can never be read as syntax. Where the variable part is a table or column name and cannot be parameterised, resolve it through a fixed allow-list of permitted identifiers rather than by escaping.
principles: Validate on an allow-list, never a deny-list.
Least privilege on the database account: a read path should not hold write rights.
preserve: The endpoint must still accept the same inputs and return the same result shape for legitimate values, including values that merely contain punctuation.
Search and filter behaviour, including partial and case-insensitive matching, must be unchanged.
common_mistakes: Blocking a keyword list (UNION, SELECT, --). Trivially bypassed by casing, comments, or encoding, and it rejects legitimate input containing those words.
Escaping quotes by hand. Misses numeric contexts and every dialect-specific escape.
Rejecting all input containing a quote. Stops the attack and breaks every surname with an apostrophe.

entries.title: Cryptographic Failures — credential storage
entries.guidance: Store credentials with a memory-hard, salted, deliberately slow password hash (argon2id, scrypt, or bcrypt), never a general-purpose digest. Generate a unique random salt per record and store it with the hash. Verify with the library's constant-time comparison.
principles: A password hash must be slow by design; a checksum is the wrong tool.
Salt per record, generated from a cryptographic source.
preserve: Existing accounts must still be able to authenticate. A change in hashing scheme that invalidates stored credentials has locked out every user.
Registration, login, and password change must all continue to work end to end.
common_mistakes: Adding a salt while keeping the fast digest. Salting defeats rainbow tables and does nothing about brute force.
Double-hashing with the same fast function. No meaningful cost increase.
Rehashing on the fly without a migration path, so old credentials silently stop verifying.
